Carry an R package library over to a new version of R

Source: R/upgrade_r_library.R
upgrade_r_library.Rd

Run this from the new R, right after installing it, to bring over the packages installed under an older R.

Usage

upgrade_r_library(
  from,
  to = .libPaths()[1],
  method = c("auto", "copy", "reinstall"),
  check = TRUE,
  dry_run = FALSE
)

Arguments

from

the old R installation (e.g., "C:/R/R-4.6.1") or one of its package libraries

to

the library to put the packages in; default: the first of .libPaths()

method

"auto" (copy for a patch upgrade, otherwise reinstall), "copy" or "reinstall"

check

test-load the packages brought over?

dry_run

if TRUE, only report what would be done

Value

A data frame, invisibly: the output of installed_pkg_sources() for the old library, with columns action (what was done) and problem (why a package failed to install or load, if it did).

Details

  • For a patch upgrade (same x.y, e.g. 4.6.1 to 4.6.2), the package folders are simply copied: packages built for one x.y.* release work in any other, so nothing needs to be downloaded or rebuilt, and packages from GitHub, r-universe, R-Forge or local files come along too.

  • For a minor or major upgrade (e.g. 4.6 to 4.7), packages must be reinstalled. Each one is reinstalled from where it originally came from (see installed_pkg_sources()): CRAN, another CRAN-like repository, R-Forge, Bioconductor or GitHub. Packages installed from local files are listed for you to reinstall by hand.

Either way, packages that the new R already has (its base and recommended packages, or anything already installed) are left alone, translations and packages built under R < 4.0 are skipped, and with check = TRUE the packages brought over are test-loaded in fresh R processes, in batches (loading 1000 packages in one session runs into the limit on loaded DLLs).

Close other R sessions using the new R first; sessions running the old R don't matter. Afterwards, outdated_pkgs() lists the packages with newer versions on CRAN.

See also

installed_pkg_sources(), outdated_pkgs(), update_pkgs(), save_installed_pkgs()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# in the newly installed R 4.6.2:
res <- upgrade_r_library("C:/R/R-4.6.1", dry_run = TRUE)   # see the plan
res <- upgrade_r_library("C:/R/R-4.6.1")
subset(res, !is.na(problem))
} # }
